measures.name: VC Investment as a Share of GDP
measures.definition: Total disclosed VC investment received by startups in the ecosystem during the year, relative to nominal GDP - the overall scale of venture funding against the size of the economy.
measures.construction: Sum of disclosed deal sizes per country-year over World Bank nominal GDP. Undisclosed rounds (~19% of deals) are excluded from the numerator. GDP denominator - country level only.
measures.caveat: PitchBook feed only (Tracxn, Zero2IPO, ATBD, Briter not yet merged), VC deals only (DealClass = "Venture Capital", no deal-status filter). Cells with fewer than 10 underlying observations are suppressed; every value ships its n. Cities are PitchBook HQ cities - municipalities, not metro areas (Palo Alto does not roll into San Francisco).

measures.name: Active VC Investors per 1,000 VC/PE-Backed Companies
measures.definition: How many distinct investors are active in the market, per thousand companies that actually raised money there - syndicate breadth rather than investor supply per startup.
measures.construction: Numerator: distinct investor IDs with a VC deal in the geography in [t-2, t]. Denominator: distinct companies headquartered there with at least one VC or PE equity financing round in the SAME window (from the full PitchBook drop, so private-equity rounds count; buyouts, secondaries, IPOs, debt and grants never make a company backed). The denominator is deliberately not "all startups": PitchBook’s universe is built around companies that raised money, so a startup-population denominator would describe something the data does not contain.
measures.caveat: PitchBook feed only (Tracxn, Zero2IPO, ATBD, Briter not yet merged), VC deals only (DealClass = "Venture Capital", no deal-status filter). Cells with fewer than 10 underlying observations are suppressed; every value ships its n. Cities are PitchBook HQ cities - municipalities, not metro areas (Palo Alto does not roll into San Francisco).

measures.name: Median Time from Founding to First VC Round
measures.definition: Median months from founding to the first observed VC round, by the year of that round - how quickly startups that do raise reach their first institutional capital.
measures.construction: First deal per company; founding dated to 1 July of the founding year (only the year exists in the feed), months = days / 30.44, negatives clipped to zero. Assigned to the year of the first round.
measures.caveat: PitchBook feed only (Tracxn, Zero2IPO, ATBD, Briter not yet merged), VC deals only (DealClass = "Venture Capital", no deal-status filter). measures.construction: Median disclosed size over GDP per head. The denominator is currently GDP per ADULT (Findex 15+ population interpolated between waves) - drop data/inputs/wdi_population.csv in to switch to true per-capita automatically. GDP denominator - country level only.
measures.caveat: PitchBook feed only (Tracxn, Zero2IPO, ATBD, Briter not yet merged), VC deals only (DealClass = "Venture Capital", no deal-status filter). measures.name: Average Number of Financing Deals per Funded Firm
measures.definition: Average number of qualifying external financing rounds received by firms that have raised external investment at least once - the depth and recurrence of private-market financing among firms that enter the funding market.
measures.construction: Firm universe: ALL firms headquartered in the ecosystem with at least one qualifying deal - no startup-age restriction. Qualifying = a new external equity financing round (angel, pre-seed/seed, VC and Series A-D+, growth equity, corporate VC, equity crowdfunding, accelerator rounds). Excluded: M&A and buyouts, IPOs and PIPEs, secondary transactions, debt and convertibles, grants, joint ventures, asset deals and duplicate round records. Published per year over a trailing five-year window so years stay comparable; the spec-exact single value over the whole 2010-2025 period ships in outputs/capital/F13_full_period.csv.
measures.caveat: PitchBook feed only (Tracxn, Zero2IPO, ATBD, Briter not yet merged), VC deals only (DealClass = "Venture Capital", no deal-status filter). Cells with fewer than 10 underlying observations are suppressed; every value ships its n. Cities are PitchBook HQ cities - municipalities, not metro areas (Palo Alto does not roll into San Francisco).

measures.name: Funding Industry Concentration
measures.definition: Concentration of VC investment across industries (Herfindahl index over industry shares of disclosed VC value). Higher = capital concentrated in fewer industries; lower = broader sectoral allocation. The three industries receiving the most deals that year travel with the value and are shown in the ecosystem panel.
measures.construction: Industry = Company.PrimaryIndustrySector from the full PitchBook drop (7 sectors, 99.6% filled). Shares are of DISCLOSED VC deal value per ecosystem-year; HHI = sum of squared shares. The top-3 list ranks industries by DEAL COUNT in the same ecosystem-year, so it answers "where did the deals go" rather than "where did the dollars go".
measures.caveat: PitchBook feed only (Tracxn, Zero2IPO, ATBD, Briter not yet merged), VC deals only (DealClass = "Venture Capital", no deal-status filter). Cells with fewer than 10 underlying observations are suppressed; every value ships its n. Cities are PitchBook HQ cities - municipalities, not metro areas (Palo Alto does not roll into San Francisco).
measures.source: PitchBook full feed PB_20260205, canonical VC deal-investor extract

measures.name: Median Time from First Investment to IPO
measures.definition: Median months from a company’s first external financing round to its IPO - how long the road to a public listing runs for the companies that get there.
measures.construction: Per company: months from its first qualifying external financing round to its IPO; median per ecosystem, keyed on the IPO year. Uses the full deal table (82,089 IPO records for 79,475 companies); the earlier VC-only extract carried 24. Cancelled and rumoured transactions are dropped. Survivorship applies by construction - only companies that DID list are in the sample, so this is the speed of realised exits, not the odds of one.
measures.caveat: PitchBook feed only (Tracxn, Zero2IPO, ATBD, Briter not yet merged), VC deals only (DealClass = "Venture Capital", no deal-status filter). Cells with fewer than 10 underlying observations are suppressed; every value ships its n. measures.name: Leading Industry Share of VC Deals
measures.definition: Which industry the deals actually go to: the share of the year’s VC deals received by the ecosystem’s single largest industry, with that industry named. A high share means one industry dominates local deal flow; the name says which.
measures.construction: Industries ranked by DEAL COUNT within each ecosystem-year using Company.PrimaryIndustryGroup - 41 groups (Software, Pharmaceuticals and Biotechnology, Commercial Services, ...), 99.6% filled - rather than F08’s 7 broad sectors, because the point of this measure is the label. Value = deals in the leading industry over all VC deals with a known industry group that year. The industry name ships with every value and appears in the rankings row, the panel headline and under each year’s bar.
measures.caveat: PitchBook feed only (Tracxn, Zero2IPO, ATBD, Briter not yet merged), VC deals only (DealClass = "Venture Capital", no deal-status filter). Cells with fewer than 10 underlying observations are suppressed; every value ships its n. Cities are PitchBook HQ cities - municipalities, not metro areas (Palo Alto does not roll into San Francisco).
measures.source: PitchBook full feed PB_20260205, canonical VC deal-investor extract

measures.name: Number of Unicorns
measures.definition: How many private companies in the ecosystem are valued at one billion dollars or more, counted at the end of each year, alongside the number newly reaching that level and the number leaving it through an IPO or acquisition. A floor rather than a total: companies that reached a billion without a publicly disclosed round valuation are not counted.
measures.construction: Entry = the first deal whose post-money valuation reaches 1,000 (PitchBook states valuations in millions of USD, so 1,000 = one billion); the year of that deal is the entry year. Exit = the first IPO or Merger/Acquisition deal dated on or after entry. A company counts in the stock from its entry year until the year it exits. Valuations marked Estimated are kept alongside Actual ones - dropping estimates roughly halves the count - and no staleness rule is applied, so a company valued at a billion in 2021 stays in the stock until it exits. Country and city are PitchBook HQ fields, and the platform’s multi-city ecosystems are summed from their member HQ cities exactly as the VC measures are.
measures.caveat: Post-money valuation is populated on 18.7% of deals, so every count is a FLOOR: a company that reached a billion without a disclosed round valuation is invisible here (outputs/unicorns/run/unicorns_valuation_coverage_by_year.csv reports the coverage year by year). Valuations are never marked down in this data, so the stock only falls through exits - the zombie-unicorn problem - and the trend rises partly for that reason; the compute script can apply a staleness rule (--stale-after-years 5) if a decaying private market should not read as a growing one. 60.7% of entrants have a recorded exit; the rest are assumed still private, and their OwnershipStatus travels in the company list so the assumption can be checked.
measures.source: PitchBook full drop CHICAGO_BOOTH_20260205 - Deal (post-money valuation, deal type, date) and Company (HQ, ownership status), unicorns run 2026-08-14

measures.name: Share of Job Postings for Technical Roles
measures.definition: Share of all job postings in the ecosystem that are engineering or technical roles - how much of local hiring demand is for the people who build the product. Postings from ALL employers, not only startups: the posting panel carries no firm-age field, so a startup-only version is not computable from this source.
measures.construction: Numerator: postings whose harmonised role label falls in the 15-role technical set (Software Engineer, Software Developer, Web Developer, Data Engineer, Data Scientist, DevOps Engineer, Systems Engineer, Test Engineer, QA Tester, Technical Support Engineer, Technical Architect, Information Security, Technology Lead, Technology Analyst, IT Project Manager) - 11.2% of the 1.59bn-posting panel. Denominator: all postings in the same place and period. The source is QUARTERLY; years are rebuilt from the posting counts (sum of technical postings over sum of all postings), never by averaging quarterly shares. Hardware roles are excluded from the headline and travel alongside as a variant. City ecosystems are Revelio metropolitan areas summed to the platform’s ecosystems (Silicon Valley = San Francisco + San Jose metros; Texas Trio = Austin + Dallas + Houston; Greater Boston = Boston + Cambridge; Mumbai = Mumbai + Navi Mumbai), again on counts.
measures.caveat: Revelio Labs LinkedIn-derived panel: coverage follows online professional profiles and job boards, so white-collar and technology roles are over-represented and the picture thins in markets where LinkedIn use is low. Cells below the measure’s minimum count are suppressed at source. City values are Revelio metropolitan areas mapped onto the platform’s ecosystems, so they are broader than the PitchBook HQ-city cuts used by the capital measures. The posting panel ends 2025-04-06, so 2025 rests on Q1 alone.
measures.source: Revelio Labs job postings panel (Revelio_job_postings_all), M080 run 2026-08-14

measures.name: Workers Moving from Large Firms to Startups
measures.definition: How many workers leave an established employer for a young firm, per thousand incumbent workers - whether experienced talent is willing to move into the startup sector.
measures.construction: A move counts when a worker’s next position is at a firm younger than 5 years, having left an employer at least 5 years old with 1,000+ employees. The destination spell must last at least 3 months, the gap between jobs at most 3 months, and transfers inside the same group are dropped. Denominator: incumbent workers in the ecosystem in the prior year. Published for 17 countries; city ecosystems are built by summing movers and incumbent workers across the member metropolitan areas.
measures.caveat: Revelio Labs LinkedIn-derived panel: coverage follows online professional profiles and job boards, so white-collar and technology roles are over-represented and the picture thins in markets where LinkedIn use is low. Cells below the measure’s minimum count are suppressed at source. City values are Revelio metropolitan areas mapped onto the platform’s ecosystems, so they are broader than the PitchBook HQ-city cuts used by the capital measures. Firm age is known for 43% of companies and headcount for 72%, so the incumbent and startup sides are both defined on the covered subset; 2025 is a partial year.
measures.source: Revelio Labs individual positions + company panel (Revelio_individual_positions_all, revelio_companies_extra_merged_map), M091 run 2026-08-14

measures.name: International Talent Flows in the Startup Sector
measures.definition: Cross-border movement into and out of the local startup sector, per thousand people already working in it: arrivals, departures and the net of the two. All three are published, because a net of +5 built from 6 arrivals and 1 departure describes a very different ecosystem from one built from 105 arrivals and 100 departures. The Flow selector switches the map between them; the ecosystem panel shows the trio together.
measures.construction: An arrival counts when a worker’s new position is in a different country from the previous one, the new firm is younger than 5 years, and the worker stays at least 6 months (open spells count as persisting). Denominator: workers already in the local startup sector the year before. Departures are counted the same way in reverse, and net = arrivals - departures, all over the same denominator. The all-employers comparison scope stays in the source file. Country level only.
measures.caveat: Revelio Labs LinkedIn-derived panel: coverage follows online professional profiles and job boards, so white-collar and technology roles are over-represented and the picture thins in markets where LinkedIn use is low. Cells below the measure’s minimum count are suppressed at source. City values are Revelio metropolitan areas mapped onto the platform’s ecosystems, so they are broader than the PitchBook HQ-city cuts used by the capital measures. A move is inferred from consecutive positions, not from visa or migration records, and 2025 is a partial year.
measures.source: Revelio Labs individual positions + company mapping (Revelio_individual_positions_all, Revelio_company_mapping_all), M094 run 2026-08-14

measures.name: Share of Workers in Technical Roles (5+ Years' Experience)
measures.definition: Share of the observed workforce that is both in a technical role and experienced in it - at least five cumulative years - so it reads the depth of the technical bench rather than its size. The denominator is EVERYONE working in the ecosystem, not only startup employees, and the five-year test is part of the definition: this is the experienced technical bench, not the headcount of technical staff.
measures.construction: Numerator: people holding a technical role during the year with at least 60 cumulative months in technical roles as at 31 December, experience summed over spells clipped to year-end and capped at the elapsed span since the first technical spell (so two concurrent jobs cannot count twice). Denominator: everyone observed working in the ecosystem that year. The technical family is the same 15-role set as hiring demand, bridged from role_k150 to its 205 role_k1500 members through the postings table. Project-local variant of M078, deliberately renamed: the experience threshold is 5 years rather than 8, there is no doctoral-qualification leg (education is recorded for about three quarters of people and the degree field for about half of those, so a PhD leg would measure profile completeness), and only the total-employment denominator is reported. City ecosystems are rebuilt from the member metros head counts.
measures.caveat: Revelio Labs LinkedIn-derived panel: coverage follows online professional profiles and job boards, so white-collar and technology roles are over-represented and the picture thins in markets where LinkedIn use is low. Cells below the measure’s minimum count are suppressed at source. City values are Revelio metropolitan areas mapped onto the platform’s ecosystems, so they are broader than the PitchBook HQ-city cuts used by the capital measures. About a quarter of technical spells have no end date and are treated as still open, so experience keeps accruing for people who left the field without updating their record - this lifts the trend more than the level, so compare ecosystems within a year before comparing an ecosystem across years. People employed in technical roles are not the AVAILABLE pool: this source carries no job-seeking signal.
measures.source: Revelio Labs individual positions (Revelio_individual_positions_all) with the role_k150 -> role_k1500 bridge from Revelio_job_postings_all, ATSD run 2026-08-14

measures.name: Change in Job Postings per Employer

variants.label: Year on year (same quarter a year earlier)

measures.definition: How fast job postings per employer are growing or shrinking - the hiring pulse of an ecosystem, held to the number of employers doing the posting rather than to raw volume. Published four ways: against the same quarter a year earlier (the headline), quarter on quarter, on a four-quarter average, and as the underlying level of postings per employer.
measures.construction: Per employer-place-quarter, the panel is collapsed so an employer posting a thousand times in a quarter counts once. Postings per employer uses a trailing four-quarter denominator - unique employers over the year - and the annual figure is taken at the LAST COMPLETE quarter of each year (Q4), where that window spans exactly the year. 2025 has only a partial first quarter and is not published as a year. All employers, no startup filter. Multi-metro ecosystems (Silicon Valley = San Francisco + San Jose, ...) are combined as employer-weighted means of their member metros, because unique employers cannot be summed across places without double-counting anyone who posts in both.
measures.caveat: Revelio Labs LinkedIn-derived panel: coverage follows online professional profiles and job boards, so white-collar and technology roles are over-represented and the picture thins in markets where LinkedIn use is low. Cells below the measure’s minimum count are suppressed at source. City values are Revelio metropolitan areas mapped onto the platform’s ecosystems, so they are broader than the PitchBook HQ-city cuts used by the capital measures. The employer count is a proxy for the active-firm count the specification asks for: it counts employers that POSTED, not employers that exist. A single quarter is noisy, which is why the four-quarter average and the year-on-year comparison ship alongside.
measures.source: Revelio Labs job postings panel (Revelio_job_postings_all), M114 run 2026-08-14

measures.name: Median Duration of Job Postings
measures.definition: How long a job advert stays up before it is taken down. Read it as friction, not as time-to-hire: the data records that a posting came down, not whether anyone was hired - filled, withdrawn, expired and reposted are indistinguishable here. Published for all roles and for the technical role set.
measures.construction: Per posting: days between the posting date and its recorded removal, taken as a median within role x place x quarter cells (the 150-role harmonised taxonomy; the finer 1,500-role rows cover the same postings and would double-count). The platform figure is the POSTING-WEIGHTED MEDIAN OF THOSE ROLE MEDIANS - the duration of the typical role, weighted by how much hiring it accounts for - because a median cannot be re-medianed and the posting-level durations are not in the published output. Same-day removals are dropped (--min-open-days 1). Multi-metro ecosystems are combined the same way, weighting their member metros by closed postings.
measures.caveat: Revelio Labs LinkedIn-derived panel: coverage follows online professional profiles and job boards, so white-collar and technology roles are over-represented and the picture thins in markets where LinkedIn use is low. Cells below the measure’s minimum count are suppressed at source. City values are Revelio metropolitan areas mapped onto the platform’s ecosystems, so they are broader than the PitchBook HQ-city cuts used by the capital measures. Three things bound this number. Removal is not hiring: in a 1% employer sample, 74.9% of closed postings were reposted by the same employer for the same role within 30 days, so most removals are not filled vacancies. Postings still open at the data cut (0.9%) are excluded, which biases the median DOWNWARD. And the vendor expires postings at 184 days, so the distribution is right-truncated - medians only, never means. The role-weighted construction is a summary of role medians, not a pooled median over postings.
measures.source: Revelio Labs job postings panel (Revelio_job_postings_all), posting and removal dates, M115 run 2026-08-14
